pillar_reactions.evidence: Asked 'Any questions on that? Does this approach, do you feel like that would actually work for you?' he answered simply 'Yeah.' No questions, no pushback. Warmer earlier in the call about the method itself, before it was formally presented — 'I've been getting more into the kettlebell workout stuff, and I was like, oh, this is really enjoyable' — but the pillar delivery itself drew only agreement.

The most engaged he was with any pillar, though still without questions. When the rep listed clean whole foods he volunteered 'Yeah, we got a couple of chickens in our backyard for that reason', which the rep rewarded warmly. Asked 'Any questions on nutrition?' the transcript records no objection and the rep moved on. He had already described a high-protein diet of red meat, fish and chicken with fruit snacking and no macro tracking, so the approach matched what he was doing.

'That sounds great.' Nothing else. He asked nothing about the weekly check-in, the video review, or the direct line to Trevor, which is notable given that never having worked with a coach is the one genuinely new thing in this offer for him.

anchors.raw: I've always had time in the past to kind of build out my own workouts or shell out a little bit for like a prepaid workout plan that you just kind of like go through on your own
anchors.note: His entire reference class for paying for fitness is 'shell out a little bit' for a self-guided plan. That is a subscription-or-less expectation sitting under a $6,000 offer, and it was never surfaced or reframed. The price was never reached on this recording, so how it would have landed is unobservable.

anchors.raw: I looked into it really This year, I don't even remember, but I decided to go a different path.
anchors.note: He has already evaluated coaching this year and chosen against it. Whatever reasoning drove that decision is still in place and was never asked about. The most useful unasked question on the call.

anchors.raw: Maybe a little over a year.
anchors.note: Following Trevor for over a year and already trying the free workouts. High practitioner trust built before the call, which is the strongest asset on the buying side and the rep did register it — 'So, all right. I think a while.' — without converting it into anything.

unmet_demand.want: Relief from cognitive rather than physical depletion — he identified mental fog after intellectually demanding days as the thing actually left on the table, not physical capacity
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asked the question that surfaced it and then never returned to it. None of the three pillars was connected to it, even though sleep, nutrition and training load are plausibly the levers. The offer was subsequently presented entirely in terms of physical efficiency and leanness, neither of which is what he said was wrong.

unmet_demand.want: Kettlebell programming knowledge specifically — 'I don't feel like I really know what I would be doing with them to optimize things'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Actually well served, and the rep positioned the six-month self-sufficiency arc directly at it. Recorded here only because the recording ends before he could react to what it costs.
